sources.entry: Demystifying bitwise operations, a gentle C tutorial

summary.title: Demystifying bitwise operations, a gentle C tutorial
summary.one_liner: You learn how number bases and binary representation work, and how to use C bitwise operators (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, shifts) with fixed-width integer types.
takeaways: Numbers are stored in binary; converting between bases uses repeated division and recording remainders.
C's fixed-width types (uint8_t to uint64_t) and their *_MAX macros give portable bit widths.
Bitwise AND, OR, XOR and NOT operate on each bit pair; XOR of identical values is zero.
Left and right shifts move bits within a number and can be used in place of powers-of-two arithmetic.
Bitwise operations are rarely needed in everyday code but matter for systems, network, embedded and performance-critical work.
summary.summary: This tutorial introduces number systems (binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal) and explains how to convert between them with repeated division. It then covers C fixed-width integer types, their maximum-value macros, and printf formats from inttypes.h. The core section walks through bitwise AND, OR, XOR, NOT and left/right shifts, with small C code examples and bit-level diagrams. The page is part of a longer article whose table of contents also lists masks, bit get/set/toggle, powers-of-two tricks, a BitSet implementation, and negative number representation, though the fetched text ends before those sections.
